title: Best Encrypted Email Providers Compared
metaDescription: Compare Proton Mail, Tuta (formerly Tutanota), StartMail, Mailfence and Guerrilla Mail on encryption, sign-up, mail-app support, storage and apps.
intro: Your Gmail account isn't as private as you think. Standard email can be read by your provider's systems, marketers track when you open messages, and unencrypted mail is exposed when an account or server is breached. An encrypted email provider protects your privacy and keeps sensitive mail secure.

products.name: Proton Mail
products.tagline: Swiss encrypted email with end-to-end encryption by default
products.pricing: Free plan; Mail Plus from about $4/month billed yearly
pros: No personal information required to sign up
The same account includes Proton Calendar, Drive and VPN
cons: Desktop mail apps need the Bridge app, which is for paid plans only

products.name: Tuta
products.tagline: German encrypted email (formerly Tutanota) that also encrypts subject lines
pros: Encrypts entire mailbox including subject lines
Based in Germany with strong privacy laws
Custom domain support on all paid plans
cons: Smaller user base than Proton Mail
No IMAP, so standard mail apps can't connect

products.name: StartMail
products.tagline: Privacy-focused email with unlimited disposable addresses
pros: No logs policy from privacy-focused company
cons: Smaller feature set compared to Proton Mail

products.name: Mailfence
products.tagline: Belgian secure email with full collaboration suite
pros: Full office suite with documents and calendar
IMAP, POP and SMTP from the Entry plan (€3.50/month)
cons: Interface feels dated compared to competitors
Encryption not automatic for all emails

products.name: Guerrilla Mail
products.tagline: Temporary disposable email addresses, no sign-up needed
pros: Can send as well as receive mail
cons: Limited functionality compared to full email services
Inbox messages are deleted after about an hour

verdict.summary: Proton Mail scores highest on this table: end-to-end encryption by default, sign-up without a phone number, custom domains on paid plans and full mobile apps, though desktop mail apps need its Bridge app, which is for paid plans only. StartMail and Tuta tie next (StartMail is listed first only because ties go alphabetically): StartMail for IMAP support, 20GB of storage and unlimited aliases, though it has no free plan or native apps; Tuta for encrypting subject lines and for its web, desktop and mobile apps, though it has no IMAP. Mailfence adds documents and a calendar, with IMAP from its Entry plan. Guerrilla Mail is a disposable inbox rather than an encrypted mail service, so it scores low on these criteria, but it is handy for one-off sign-ups.

pro_tips: Use a private window when you check your email on a shared or public computer, and sign out when you finish, so your login session isn't left saved or cached.
Enable two-factor authentication on your encrypted email account - even the most secure providers benefit from this additional security layer.
Create email aliases or use disposable addresses when signing up for services to prevent your main encrypted email from being exposed in data breaches.
Gradually migrate your important accounts to your new encrypted email rather than switching everything at once - this helps you identify which services really need the extra security.
Keep your old email account active for a few months after switching to catch any important messages you might have missed during the transition process.

faqs.question: Can I send encrypted emails to people using Gmail or other regular email providers?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the level of encryption varies. Proton Mail, Tuta and StartMail can send password-protected messages to any email address. For full end-to-end encryption, both parties need to use the same encrypted email service or compatible PGP encryption.

faqs.question: Will switching to encrypted email make me look suspicious?
faqs.answer: Not at all. Millions of professionals, journalists, and privacy-conscious individuals use encrypted email daily. It's becoming standard practice for anyone handling sensitive information, and major companies increasingly expect secure communications.

faqs.question: How difficult is it to migrate from Gmail to an encrypted email provider?
faqs.answer: Most encrypted email providers offer migration tools to import your existing emails and contacts. The process typically takes a few hours to complete, and you can run both accounts simultaneously during the transition period.

faqs.question: Do encrypted email providers work with my current email apps like Outlook or Apple Mail?
faqs.answer: It depends on the provider. StartMail supports IMAP on every plan and Mailfence from its Entry plan, so they work with standard email clients. Proton Mail needs its Bridge app, available on paid plans, for desktop clients, and Tuta works only with its own web, desktop and mobile apps.

faqs.question: Are free encrypted email plans sufficient for most users?
faqs.answer: Free plans from Proton Mail and Tuta provide solid encryption and privacy protection suitable for personal use. You'll mainly need paid plans for more storage, custom domains, or advanced features like email aliases and priority support.

faqs.question: Can law enforcement or governments access my encrypted emails?
faqs.answer: Reputable encrypted email providers store your mail encrypted so that they cannot read it, even if compelled by authorities. However, mail from ordinary providers reaches their servers unencrypted before it is stored, and metadata like sender and recipient addresses and timestamps may still be accessible depending on the provider's jurisdiction and policies.
